signals.title: AUD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Shock
signals.text: AUD/JPY faces sharp downside into the open as JPY 1W outperformance (+1.821%, n=7) collides with extreme AUD weakness (-2.688%, n=4), generating a 4.509% G10 bilateral spread. Middle East escalation following naval mine strikes east of the Strait of Hormuz and equity liquidations trigger safe-haven JPY demand that overrides AUD's +362bp OIS carry advantage (AONIA 4.85% vs TONA 1.23%). The Sydney open and subsequent Tokyo cash session resolve whether safe-haven demand breaks support toward 103.50. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/JPY into the open as safe-haven flows dominate carry. Catalyst: Sydney/Tokyo market open following Strait of Hormuz conflict escalation. Risk: Immediate geopolitical de-escalation or Strait reopening announcement driving a relief rally above 106.00.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Long Unwind & Technical Breakdown
signals.text: AUD/USD closed Friday at 0.6619 as leveraged funds cut net long exposure by 15,052 contracts to +26,143, accelerating downside momentum. Deteriorating Australian macro data (ESI -9.6) and technical breakdown below all key daily moving averages (extended 5.62 ATR below SMA20 at 0.6883) reinforce selling pressure despite AUD's 94bp OIS carry advantage over USD. The next RBA meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) on 8 Dec determines whether current hold expectations hold or shift to an outright dovish tilt. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD on persistent positioning liquidation. Catalyst: Sydney open and RBA meeting on 8 Dec. Risk: Shift in Federal Reserve rate path expectations or rebound in commodity demand pushing spot back above 0.6700.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Short Squeeze & BoC Divergence
signals.text: CAD COT LF net short of -75,447 contracts (22.5% long) anchors USD/CAD upside after spot closed Friday at 1.4340. signals.title: USD/JPY — Safe-Haven Surge & Volatility Risk
signals.text: USD/JPY closed Friday at 158.51 as surging risk-off demand drives 1M risk reversals to -1.77 and expands implied volatility premium (IV 7.5% vs HV30 5.3%, VRP +2.2%). Speculative JPY shorts (-29,545 contracts, 85th percentile) face squeeze risk if Strait of Hormuz supply disruptions accelerate broader equity liquidation. The next BoJ meeting (mkt: 77% hike priced) on 18 Dec determines whether domestic normalization pace quickens. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY targeting downside squeeze toward 156.50. signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Speculative Short & PMI Risk
signals.text: EUR COT LF net short stands at an extreme -105,891 contracts (30.4% long, 2nd percentile, z=-1.68), leaving EUR/USD vulnerable to a short squeeze from Friday's close at 1.0975. Subdued European macro performance and a 147bp OIS carry penalty (SOFR 3.91% vs €STR 2.44%) keep spot below all key moving averages, but crowded positioning limits aggressive downside extension. Monday's Flash Eurozone PMIs serve as the immediate directional test. Trade bias: Neutral-to-bearish EUR/USD with caution on crowded short unwinds. Catalyst: Eurozone Flash Manufacturing and Services PMIs at 09:00 UTC Monday. Risk: Upside surprise in German and Eurozone PMIs above 52.0 triggering a squeeze back to the 1.1115 SMA20 level.
